title: Localization and boundary comparison for a closed section with a retraction
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $p:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism, and let $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed section, so $ps=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be its quasi-compact open complement and put $\pi=pj$. The meanings of these morphisms are [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. For each scheme $T$ write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and put $K=\nu_X^*B$, in the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], where $D^+$ denotes objects whose cohomology sheaves vanish below some integer. Use the finite direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Use the finite-level transported exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and put $C=Rs^!K\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

There is a natural distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$C\longrightarrow Rp_*K\longrightarrow R\pi_*j^*K\xrightarrow{d}C[1].$$
It is the $\nu_Y^*$-transport of the ordinary etale closed-support localization triangle after $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$, with $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}s_*s^\times B=s^\times B$. The finite direct-image comparison identifies the second arrow with restriction along $j$. Here $s^\times$ is the ordinary etale right adjoint of $s_*$, and the first arrow is the image of its counit, with the transported exceptional functor and counit identified by the compactification $Y\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Y\xrightarrow{s}X$. These identifications are natural in $B$ and use the canonical etale/pro-etale direct-image comparisons, rather than an adjunction on all pro-etale inputs.

Use cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and supported cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Applying derived global sections to this triangle identifies $H^{q+1}(Y,C)$ with $H^{q+1}_{s(Y)}(X,K)$ and identifies $H^q(Y,d)$ with the support boundary $\partial:H^q(U,j^*K)\to H^{q+1}_{s(Y)}(X,K)$ of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. For the canonical edge maps $e_V^r:H^r(Y,V)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^r(V))$ and the cohomology-sheaf boundary $\delta^q:\mathcal H^q(R\pi_*j^*K)\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(C)$, one has, for every integer $q$ and $\alpha\in H^q(U,j^*K)$,
$$e_C^{q+1}(\partial\alpha)=\Gamma(Y,\delta^q)\bigl(e_{R\pi_*j^*K}^{q}(\alpha)\bigr).$$
The edge maps here send a global cohomology class to its local cohomology classes in the cohomology sheaf. The boundary and all these identifications agree with their ordinary etale counterparts under site comparison.
